Let \(s=\sqrt c\) and \(t=\sqrt{b+\sqrt c}=\sqrt{b+s}\). Then \(x=a+t\).

First note \(t\notin \mathbb Q(s)\). If \(t\in\mathbb Q(s)\), write \(t=u+vs\) with \(u,v\in\mathbb Q\) and \(2uv=1\). Since \(x\) is an algebraic integer, \(n=2u\in\mathbb Z\) and \(v=1/n\). The minimal polynomial of \(x\) is
\[
x^2-Nx+D,\qquad N=2a+n,\quad D=\frac{N^2}{4}-\frac{c}{n^2}\in\mathbb Z.
\]
Dividing \(P(x)\) by this quadratic gives quotient \(x^2+(N-20)x+q\), so
\[
qD=9,\qquad q=N^2-20N+108-D.
\]
Thus
\[
N^2-20N+108=D+\frac9D.
\]
The left side is \((N-10)^2+8\ge 8\), while the right side is at most \(10\), and equality can only happen for \(D=1,9\), giving \((N-10)^2=2\), impossible. Hence \(t\notin\mathbb Q(s)\).

Therefore \(\{1,s,t,st\}\) is linearly independent over \(\mathbb Q\). Now expand:
\[
P(a+t)=(4a-20)t^3+(6a^2-60a+108+2b)t^2+(4a^3-60a^2+216a-k)t
+a^4-20a^3+108a^2-ka+9-b^2+c.
\]
Using \(t^2=b+s\), this becomes
\[
(4a-20)st+\bigl((4a-20)b+4a^3-60a^2+216a-k\bigr)t
+\bigl(6a^2-60a+108+2b\bigr)s+\cdots=0.
\]
By linear independence,
\[
4a-20=0,\qquad 6a^2-60a+108+2b=0.
\]
Thus \(a=5\), \(b=21\). The \(t\)-coefficient gives
\[
4a^3-60a^2+216a-k=0 \implies k=80.
\]
The constant term gives
\[
a^4-20a^3+108a^2-ka+9-b^2+c=0,
\]
so
\[
625-2500+2700-400+9-441+c=0 \implies c=7.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\boxed{7}
\]
